literal: Even though having learned many good things, becoming good of mind is impossible for enemies.
translation: Even when they have learned many good and noble things, it is impossible for those who harbor hostility to become pure of heart.
modern: பல நல்ல விஷயங்களைக் கற்றறிந்த போதிலும், பகைவர்கள் மனத்தால் நல்லவர்களாக மாறுவது அரிதானது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the difficulty of reforming a hostile mind through mere education. The word 'மாணார்' refers to enemies or those who do not align in true friendship. Even if such people have studied many good and noble books ('பலநல்ல கற்றக் கடைத்து'), their inner nature remains unchanged. The poet emphasizes that external learning does not automatically result in a good heart ('மனநல்லர் ஆகுதல்'), making it dangerous to trust them based solely on their education.
